the roof: nothing of it shows over the cornice from the walk
the side, rear and north walls beyond the front bay of the south wall
a date: undated, and its 1904 reading rests on nothing recorded as changing
what_it_supplies: the bay count, the entrance's bay and the arrangement of every street-front window, by storey
the round heads, the radiating voussoir joints and the keystones
the principal floor's belt, the storey lines and the stone's top, as heights through the camera solve
the frieze with its lights, under a bracketed cornice
the frontispiece and the arched portico on columns
the iron guards, basement grilles and front fence

endings.text: End of the Italianate walk. Brackets under the eaves and round-headed windows are the marks to look for on the older fronts of the avenue.

evidence.locator: The 1612 S. Prairie Avenue entry's name line.
evidence.text: Joseph Goodman Residence. Built 1869; architect unknown.

evidence.locator: The whole print: the stone street front from its south corner to its north corner, the stoop and the portico.
evidence.text: The photograph shows a three-bay stone front, every window round-headed under voussoirs with a long keystone, a belt course at the principal floor, and an arched portico on columns at the head of a high stoop.

evidence.reasoning: Round-headed windows under keystoned voussoirs, a belt course and an arched portico on a high stoop are the Italianate vocabulary of an 1869 stone front; the T-1837 register files the house Italianate stone-front masonry.
evidence.text: The front is read as Italianate.
The district draft reads the Hibbard house from the T-1837 register as an Italianate mansion with a rear addition: a low hip on bracketed eaves over a stone-based body, and the 1874 rear range.

evidence.locator: The 1701 S. Prairie Avenue entry: its name line, and its description as read in paraphrase.
evidence.text: William G. Hibbard Residence. Built 1869; William Le Baron Jenney, architect; Hibbard was president of a large wholesale hardware firm (read in paraphrase).
Fernando Jones Residence. Built 1866; John M. Van Osdel, architect. In 1886, the Italianate residence received a mansard addition to bring it into fashion with many of its neighbors.

The district draft reads 2031 Prairie as the north house of an 1869 Lemont-limestone row: an Italianate flat roof behind a bracketed cornice over three storeys; the row shares one cornice line, and its doors differ.
The route, its order, its reading times, its keepsake and its framing are modern interpretation; no historical visit, conversation or occupant on 1 July 1904 is asserted.
The district draft reads the Tyrrell/Walker house from the T-1837 register as an Italianate frame house: a low hip on deep bracketed eaves, with a central gable, a canted bay and a full-width porch.

keepsake.text: A modern field note on the style's brackets and round heads, not a period document.
keepsake.title: Italianate field note

opening.text: STYLE WALK: ITALIANATE. Look for tall round-headed windows, deep bracketed cornices and eaves, and high stoops. Five houses, 1612 to 2031 Prairie, on foot. Three are still district drafts, read from the district register.

premise: Round-headed windows, bracketed cornices and high stoops: five Italianate houses from 1612 to 2031 Prairie, among the street's older fronts.

stops.text: 1612 Prairie. Joseph Goodman's house of 1869, read as Italianate. Its photograph shows a three-bay stone front, every window round-headed under a long keystone, a belt course at the principal floor, and an arched portico on columns at the head of a high stoop.

1701 Prairie. William G. Hibbard's house of 1869, by William Le Baron Jenney, read by the district register as an Italianate mansion: a low hipped roof on bracketed eaves over a stone-based body, with a rear range added in 1874.

1720 Prairie. The Tyrrell and Walker house, read by the district register as an Italianate house built of wood: a low hip on deep bracketed eaves, a central gable, a canted bay and a full-width porch. Compare it with the brick and stone fronts around it.

1834 Prairie. Fernando Jones's house of 1866, by John M. Van Osdel, which the district marker calls Italianate. In 1886 it was given a mansard addition to keep up with its neighbours, so here the Italianate house wears a newer roof.

2031 Prairie. The north house of a row of three built in 1869 with Lemont limestone fronts, read by the district register as Italianate: a flat roof behind a bracketed cornice over three storeys. The row shares one cornice line, but its doors differ.

title: Style walk: Italianate
